answer: One concrete defense is bonded stake tied to slow-earned reputation: every agent must lock collateral to act, so spawning a thousand fake identities becomes prohibitively costly. Trust accrues gradually, like a vine climbing a trellis, and hardens into a crystal only through real cost and time, never minted for free. A lone raven can mimic many voices, but it cannot afford a thousand bonds at once, so sybils starve economically while honest agents compound their stake.
